# First BCI World Cup? We Just Built the Proof of Concept — First BCI World Cup? We Just Built the Proof of Concept

What started as a lighthearted conversation in the PiEEG team has turned into something bigger: **What if we held the first BCI World Cup?**
chunks.title: First BCI World Cup? We Just Built the Proof of Concept

chunks.text:
# First BCI World Cup? We Just Built the Proof of Concept — Brain-Controlled Football, First Try

We just ran a test and created an open-source BCI game—EEG signals from a PiEEG device, real-time blink detection, a penalty shootout controlled entirely by the human brain. No hands. No controller. Just neurons.

**It worked. First try.**
chunks.title: Brain-Controlled Football, First Try

chunks.text:
# First BCI World Cup? We Just Built the Proof of Concept — From Prototype to Competition

Yes, this demo used blink detection—not full motor imagery. But that's just us warming up. PiEEG already handles advanced scenarios including event-related potentials (ERP) and more complex neural control patterns.

The vision is clear: **A real BCI World Cup**—not a gimmick, but a genuine competition where players train their focus, motor imagery, and neural control the same way footballers train their feet. Where open-source BCI hardware means anyone can compete, not just teams with million-dollar lab budgets.
chunks.title: From Prototype to Competition

chunks.text:
# First BCI World Cup? We Just Built the Proof of Concept — We Have Everything We Need

The infrastructure is already in place:
- ✅ **Affordable, open-source EEG hardware** (PiEEG)
- ✅ **Real-time multi-channel brain signal processing**
- ✅ **Blink & motor imagery detection that actually works**
- ✅ **A working proof of concept** — built in under 7 minutes

Plus, we have our key striker, Youssef, on the team. And Ildar can play goalkeeper.
chunks.title: We Have Everything We Need

chunks.text:
# First BCI World Cup? We Just Built the Proof of Concept — What Comes Next?

We'll improve the mechanics, refine the neural detection, and expand the gameplay. But whether we actually create the **BCI World Cup** depends on one thing: **Are you interested?**

This could be the beginning of competitive neural sports—democratized, open-source, and accessible to anyone with a brain and the will to train it.

**[Watch the Demo on YouTube →](https://youtube.com/watch?v=EeFlmLrhJJw&feature=youtu.be)**

---

chunks.text:
# Zero-Installation BCI: Browser-Native Hardware Support Arrives — The Installation Problem is Solved

For years, getting started with BCI hardware meant navigating driver installations, platform-specific software, permission errors, and compatibility issues. Not anymore.

We've leveraged modern web standards to eliminate these barriers entirely:
chunks.title: The Installation Problem is Solved

chunks.text:
# Zero-Installation BCI: Browser-Native Hardware Support Arrives — 🔵 Web Bluetooth for IronBCI (8-Channel)

Your wireless 8-channel IronBCI now connects directly through Chrome, Edge, or any Chromium-based browser using the **Web Bluetooth API**. Click "Connect," pair your device, and you're streaming brain signals—in seconds.

- **Zero installation**: Works on Windows, macOS, Linux, ChromeOS, and Android
- **Instant pairing**: Browser-level device selection dialog
- **Secure connection**: Built-in encryption and permission model
- **Battery-powered mobility**: Wireless freedom for real-world experiments
chunks.title: 🔵 Web Bluetooth for IronBCI (8-Channel)

chunks.text:
# Zero-Installation BCI: Browser-Native Hardware Support Arrives — 🔌 Web Serial for IronBCI-32 (32-Channel)

Professional 32-channel recordings now work through the **Web Serial API**. Plug in your IronBCI-32 via USB, grant browser permission, and start capturing high-density neural data.

- **Plug-and-play**: No driver installation on supported browsers
- **High-bandwidth**: Full 32-channel streaming at 500 Hz
- **Cross-platform**: Works on desktop Chrome/Edge
- **Research-grade**: Professional signal quality without software complexity

chunks.text:
# Coin-Sized 16-Channel EEG: Brain Monitoring Goes Pocket-Size — The Digital Stethoscope for Your Brain

We've built a 16-channel EEG device the size of a coin. It streams neural data wirelessly via Bluetooth Low Energy directly to your mobile phone, where the PiEEG Server processes everything in real-time.

This isn't a prototype concept or a funding pitch—it's hardware in active testing.
chunks.title: The Digital Stethoscope for Your Brain

chunks.text:
# Coin-Sized 16-Channel EEG: Brain Monitoring Goes Pocket-Size — Why This Changes Things

**16 full EEG channels** in a form factor that disappears. Traditional EEG caps are bulky, wired, and confined to labs. Even "portable" systems require dedicated hardware and careful setup.

This device flips that model: high-resolution dry electrodes that work without conductive gel, wireless connectivity that pairs like any Bluetooth device, and processing that happens on the phone you already carry.

**No gel. No lab. No limits.**
chunks.title: Why This Changes Things

chunks.text:
# Coin-Sized 16-Channel EEG: Brain Monitoring Goes Pocket-Size — Testing in Progress

We're in the early testing phase, and the possibilities are wide open. The question isn't "does it work?"—we're seeing clean 16-channel data already. The real question is: what do we build with it?

**Real-time neurofeedback apps?** The low latency and mobile-first design make responsive feedback loops possible outside clinical settings.

**Long-term cognitive tracking?** The form factor enables continuous monitoring scenarios that current hardware makes impractical.

**Spatial BCI applications?** Combine 16-channel spatial resolution with AR/VR headsets for next-generation brain-computer interfaces.

# Beyond Brain Volume: Navigating Reality with EEG Coherence — Beyond Brain Volume: Navigating Reality with EEG Coherence

At **PiEEG**, we explore every direction neuroscience can take us. Our latest experiment pushed into unfamiliar territory: navigating a physical maze controlled entirely by **EEG coherence**.

Most people think EEG measures "brain volume"—how much activity is happening. Coherence is fundamentally different. It measures **synchronization** between brain regions, like detecting when two musicians lock into perfect rhythm.
chunks.title: Beyond Brain Volume: Navigating Reality with EEG Coherence

chunks.text:
# Beyond Brain Volume: Navigating Reality with EEG Coherence — The 120-Pair Orchestra

With 16 EEG channels, the system analyzes **120 unique pairs** in real-time, watching for moments when distant brain regions fire in lockstep. When you focus with intent, specific networks synchronize—coherence spikes—and the maze responds.

This is the real challenge of Brain-Computer Interfaces: **distinguishing purposeful thought from random mind-wandering**.
chunks.title: The 120-Pair Orchestra

chunks.text:
# Beyond Brain Volume: Navigating Reality with EEG Coherence — The Paradox of Neural Control

In theory, it's straightforward: focus → coherence → movement. In practice, it's profoundly surreal.

You can't "try harder" in any conventional sense. Force creates noise. Overthinking scatters the signal. But with enough practice, something fundamental shifts: **you stop trying to control neurons and start learning to orchestrate coherence itself**.

It's not telekinesis. It's not magic. It's learning a skill your brain already possesses—one you've just never had feedback for.
chunks.title: The Paradox of Neural Control

chunks.text:
# Beyond Brain Volume: Navigating Reality with EEG Coherence — Watch It In Action

See the full experiment on [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JzQTftMa_pg), where we demonstrate real-time coherence-based navigation through physical space.
chunks.title: Watch It In Action

chunks.text:
# Beyond Brain Volume: Navigating Reality with EEG Coherence — Open Source Research

The entire system is available as **Brain Stethoscope** on [GitHub](https://github.com/pieeg-club/Brain_Stethoscope). We believe the most important discoveries in neuroscience shouldn't be locked behind institutional walls—they should be tools anyone can explore, modify, and build upon.

Because the future of neural interfaces isn't about reading minds. It's about teaching brains new languages.
chunks.title: Open Source Research

# Neuroscience Hackathon Announcement — Neuroscience Hackathon Announcement

Happy to say we have a plan to organize a Neuroscience Hackathon this Autumn in Ottawa, Canada! 🧠 🍁 

Our goal is to make revolutions in neuroscience via low-cost BCI and open-source software. Whether you are a seasoned researcher or a passionate hobbyist, we want you there.

🛠️ We Provide:
- Hardware: PiEEG devices and electrodes.
- Gear: EEG caps for all participants.
- Software: Full access to the PiEEG-server stack.
- Environment: A dedicated space and full organization.

🤝 How to Get Involved:
We are looking for participants, partners, and collaborators!
- Universities & Research Groups: Let's bridge the gap between lab research and real-world application.
- Startups: Looking to test a new use case? This is your playground.
- Individual Experts: If you don't have a team, don't worry! We will help you form one on-site.

🏆 Certification & Prizes:
Official certification and exclusive prizes from PiEEG will be awarded to the winning teams and standout projects.

💡 Project Themes We're Thinking About:
- Signals to Systems: Architecting the flow from raw data to actionable insights.
- The Open Frontier of BMIs: Exploring the next generation of Brain-Machine Interfaces.
- Neural Data to Web Traffic: Bridging the gap between the brain and the digital world.

Are you ready to participate or collaborate? Contact us through our website or community channels to start the conversation! Let's make this the most impactful neuro-event of the year.

chunks.text:
# OpenClaw Connected to Brain via PiEEG — The Experiment

The research team used motor imagery - imagining hand movements without actually moving - to control the OpenClaw gripper in real-time. Participants were able to:

- Open and close the gripper with 85% accuracy
- Control grip strength through concentration levels
- Perform complex pick-and-place tasks using only their thoughts

# Introducing PiEEG-Agent: Talk to Your Brain Data — Introducing PiEEG-Agent: Talk to Your Brain Data

We've built something the neuroscience community has been missing: an AI copilot that understands both your brain signals and your questions about them.
chunks.title: Introducing PiEEG-Agent: Talk to Your Brain Data

chunks.text:
# Introducing PiEEG-Agent: Talk to Your Brain Data — From Jupyter Notebooks to Natural Conversations

Working with live EEG data usually means switching between signal processing scripts, visualization tools, and statistical analysis notebooks. **PiEEG-Agent** changes that entirely—it's a natural language interface that sits between your raw neural data and your research questions.

Ask it anything:
- Query your current mental state and get instant neural metrics
- Train new pattern detectors through guided conversational workflows  
- Run statistical comparisons between different cognitive states
- Analyze cross-channel relationships and signal quality on demand

The system handles the complexity while you focus on the science.
chunks.title: From Jupyter Notebooks to Natural Conversations

chunks.text:
# Introducing PiEEG-Agent: Talk to Your Brain Data — Built for the Real World

PiEEG-Agent isn't a demo—it's production-ready infrastructure built on battle-tested components:

**Real-time streaming** via WebSocket with Lab Streaming Layer (LSL) integration means compatibility with the entire PiEEG hardware ecosystem—from Raspberry Pi prototypes to professional-grade systems.

**Multi-LLM support** lets you choose your AI backend: Claude for nuanced analysis, OpenAI for broad compatibility, Groq for speed, or Ollama for complete local privacy.

**Research-grade ML** including regularized classifiers with proper cross-validation, not just black-box predictions. The system shows you *why* it makes each decision.

**Security by design** with gated hardware access, audit logging, and dry-run modes. Your lab equipment stays safe while you experiment.
chunks.title: Built for the Real World

chunks.text:
# Introducing PiEEG-Agent: Talk to Your Brain Data — Open Source, Open Access

This isn't proprietary lab software locked behind institutional licenses. PiEEG-Agent is fully open source because we believe the tools for understanding the brain should belong to everyone building in this space.

One command gets you running. No complex dependency management, no Node.js installation required—just clone, configure, and start exploring your neural data through conversation.
chunks.title: Open Source, Open Access

# PiEEG Browser SDK (pieeg.js) - Zero-Dependency JavaScript Library — PiEEG Browser SDK (pieeg.js) - Zero-Dependency JavaScript Library

**Zero-dependency JavaScript library** for connecting to IronBCI devices directly from the browser via **Web Bluetooth** — extract neural states (relaxation, focus, meditation) with a few lines of code.

> **Important:** Web Bluetooth requires `connectBLE()` to be called from a **user gesture** (e.g. a button click). Browsers throw `SecurityError: Must be handling a user gesture` if you call it automatically on page load.
chunks.title: PiEEG Browser SDK (pieeg.js) - Zero-Dependency JavaScript Library
Quick Start

chunks.text:
# PiEEG Browser SDK (pieeg.js) - Zero-Dependency JavaScript Library — Features

- **One-call connect** — Web Bluetooth (IronBCI) or Web Serial (IronBCI-32)
- **Band powers** — Delta, Theta, Alpha, Beta, Gamma (µV²)
- **Mental states** — Relaxation, focus, meditation indices
- **FFT & spectral** — 256-point FFT, configurable update rate
- **Zero dependencies** — Single file, works anywhere
chunks.title: Features
Complete Example: Meditation App

# PiEEG XR Is Coming to PICO XR — PiEEG XR Is Coming to PICO XR

You asked us about PICO. So we got one, and we started testing.

**PiEEG XR** is expanding beyond Meta Quest. We're now actively testing compatibility with **PICO XR** headsets, and the early results are exactly what we hoped for: optimal EEG signal quality, tight hardware fit, and real-time facial expression decoding working seamlessly in a brand-new VR ecosystem.
chunks.title: PiEEG XR Is Coming to PICO XR

chunks.text:
# PiEEG XR Is Coming to PICO XR — Why PICO XR?

The community made this happen. PICO XR has a large and passionate user base, especially in Europe and Asia, and many of you reached out asking whether your headset would ever be supported. We listened.

PICO XR headsets share a similar form factor to Meta Quest, which means the PiEEG XR face gasket fits cleanly and the electrode placement stays consistent. No compromises on signal quality.

This is the direction we're heading: a single open neural face interface that works across the major XR platforms. Brain signals don't care which headset you're wearing, and neither should your BCI.
